ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The driving point impedance \(Z(s)\) of a network has the pole-zero locations shown in the figure. If \(Z(0)=3\), what is the expression for \(Z(s)\)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a pole-zero plot in the s-plane, with the horizontal axis Re and the vertical axis Im. There is an open circle on the real axis at s=-3, representing a zero; there is a cross at each position with real part -1 and imaginary part +1 and -1, representing two poles, namely s=-1+j and s=-1-j. Reasoning: From the zero and poles, write Z(s)=K(s+3)/[(s+1-j)(s+1+j)]. The denominator simplifies to (s+1)^2+1=s^2+2s+2, so Z(s)=K(s+3)/(s^2+2s+2). From the condition Z(0)=3, K*3/2=3, therefore K=2. Thus Z(s)=2(s+3)/(s^2+2s+2).
